PhD Graduate Assistantship in Wildlife Ecology and Management
Department of Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology
University of Minnesota

Project description: The successful candidate will work with John Fieberg (https://sites.google.com/a/umn.edu/fieberg-lab/) and Todd Arnold (https://sites.google.com/a/umn.edu/fieberg-lab/) at the University of Minnesota and researchers at the Minnesota DNR to evaluate feasibility of implementing a multi-species camera-based occupancy survey for carnivores.  The student will explore questions related to study design and analysis approach using a mix of field work, simulation modeling, and analysis of camera trap data.

Prerequisites: Ideal candidates will have a MS in statistics with an interest in wildlife ecology, or a MS in fisheries, ecology, biology, or related field with a strong quantitative background. Preference will be given to those with knowledge of carnivore ecology and management, those that have experience with occupancy modeling, Bayesian methods, and program R, and those that have published quantitative ecological research.  Competitive applicants will have undergraduate and graduate GPAs > 3.4 and quantitative GRE scores that average around the 70th percentile or higher, and a GRE analytical writing score >= 4.0.  Students must have or acquire a valid US driver’s license.

Start date: September 2015 (preferred), though January 2016 may be an option. 

Stipend: Approximately $21,000 per year, plus health insurance and tuition.

To be considered for this position, send the following (preferably in a single pdf) to John Fieberg (jfie...@umn.edu):

(1) Letter of interest summarizing your experience
(2) CV or resume
(3) College transcripts (unofficial copies are fine)
(4) GRE scores (unofficial copies are fine)

Screening of applicants will begin immediately and continue until a successful candidate is found.
